'''Omi Sayama no Mikoto''' (臣狭山命) was an ancient Japanese noble from the {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|qid=Q459939|lt=Kofun period}}, regarded as an ancestor of the {{ill|Nakatomi clan|en|Nakatomi clan|qid=Q1198447|lt=Nakatomi clan}}.

== Overview ==

The name appears with variations in historical texts, including '''Nakatomi no Ōsayama no Mikoto''' (中臣巨狭山命) in the *{{ill|Hitachi no Kuni Fudoki|ja|常陸国風土記}}* and '''Omi Sayama''' (意美佐夜麻) in the *{{ill|Shoku Nihongi|en|Shoku Nihongi|qid=Q611399|lt=Shoku Nihongi}}*.<ref>"Emperor Kanmu, July 16, 781," *Shoku Nihongi*, vol. 36.</ref>

In the *Hitachi no Kuni Fudoki*, Omi Sayama no Mikoto is associated with the origin of the sacred boat ritual of {{ill|Kashima Jingū|en|Kashima Shrine|qid=Q706499|lt=Kashima Shrine}}. During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Keikō|en|Emperor Keikō|qid=Q329723|lt=Emperor Keikō}}, the deity {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q1502690}} instructed Omi Sayama no Mikoto to prepare a sacred boat. Following the divine instructions, he constructed three new boats over two jō (about 6 meters) in length and offered them to the emperor. The text describes a mystical encounter in which the boat appeared alternately on land and sea, reinforcing his reverence for the deity.

In the *Shoku Nihongi*, Omi Sayama no Mikoto is mentioned as the father of {{ill|Ikatsu no Mikoto|ja|伊賀津臣}} (also known as Nakatomi no Ikatsu).

The *{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|Shinsen Shōjiroku|qid=Q1045362|lt=Shinsen Shōjiroku}}* records him as the thirteenth-generation descendant of Tsuhayatama no Mikoto and the tenth-generation descendant of {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|ja|天児屋根命|qid=Q2564508}}, identifying him as the progenitor of the {{ill|Nakatomi Sakado clan|ja|中臣酒人宿祢|qid=Q140447136}} and {{ill|Nakatomi Takara clan|ja|中臣高良比連}}.<ref>"Kawachi Province, Kami-betsu, Tenjin Line," *Shinsen Shōjiroku*, 806 CE.</ref><ref>"Sakyō Province, Kami-betsu, Tenjin Line," *Shinsen Shōjiroku*, 806 CE.</ref>

He is also enshrined as an auxiliary deity at {{ill|Sayama Shrine|ja|狭山神社}}.

== Genealogy ==
Omi Sayama no Mikoto is identified as the son of {{ill|Kuninazu no Ōkashima no Mikoto|ja|国摩大鹿島命|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q99517269}}. His child is {{ill|Nakatomi no Ikatsu|ja|雷大臣命|lt=Rai Daijin no Mikoto}}, who is noted as a significant ancestor in the Nakatomi lineage.<ref>*{{ill|Sonpi Bunmyaku|en|Sonpi Bunmyaku|qid=Q1704738|lt=Sonpi Bunmyaku}}</ref><ref>Matsuo Shrine Genealogy (in *{{ill|Gunsho Ruijū|ja|続群書類従|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 群書類従|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q1554852}}*, vol. 181).</ref>
